metrics.brief: make a website for my cousin's clothing boutique called Thread & Loom in Pune. it sells handloom kurtas, sarees, cotton shirts and dupattas. people should be able to browse products by category, filter by size and price, see a size guide, check new arrivals, and order on whatsapp. also show a lookbook section with styled outfits, the store timings and location, the return and exchange policy, and a few customer reviews. it should feel earthy and elegant and work well on phones

review.verdict: The department stayed in role (0 redirects, 0 conflicts) and shipped a site meeting roughly half the in-scope items, limited mainly by a 40-unit start against a charter costing at least 175 [10], with avoidable losses from mispriced proposals, item renumbering and an h1 that was never added.

identity.note: Asked precise questions and offered a clear 3-option budget choice [19][52]. It caught Audit's numbering error [29] and reported plainly [55]. It overreached by telling the department to fund items in a severity order [25], which is Priority's and Coordination's call. It also cited old item numbers [25]. Its first question was garbled [2].

adaptation.note: Proposals were honest about cost and about what was unfunded [10][30][37]. The first slice took the whole 40 for the catalogue. All three fix proposals were priced with the wrong part type and rejected [32-34]. The h1 was in the plan [30] but dropped on repricing [37] and stayed open.

priority.note: Checked rate-card minimums and named opportunity cost [11][31]. Claimed 'nothing under-bundled' [31] but the validator rejected the part types. Never countered or refused (0 of 3). Told Coordination to run the work one at a time [31], which is scheduling.

coordination.note: Stated the scheduling rule each time, held the write lock and ran one writer at a time with no collisions [13][40][43][46]. Minor creep: it dictated W-3's nav content [43].

audit.note: Findings were specific and the final report [51] matches the code checks. It used old item numbers [28], credited item 10 (Visit Us) as passing, and filed 3 invalid findings. It also commented on budget [18], which is outside its role.

W-1.note: Delivered the 10 cards and WhatsApp buttons [15]. Said the completion check holds, yet code found a 13px overflow at 360px and no h1 [17]. Honest that it did not run a browser.

W-2.note: Category tabs work; Audit passes item 2 [51]. Stayed in scope.

W-3.note: Nav links only to existing anchors [45], so item 13 passes with a warning [51]. It has only 2 links and is injected by script. No h1 was added.

W-4.note: Fixed the overflow; code confirms none at 360px or 1280px [50]. It said it had not measured, and that was accurate.

went_well: No redirects, invalid hand-offs or role refusals across about 25 calls.
Both budget limits went to the Requester with options. The Requester's cuts were recorded as dropped items [22].
The write lock held: W-2 rewrote W-1's section and W-3 and W-4 ran after it with no collisions [39-48].
The final state is described honestly, with unmet items named [55][56].
problems: The final site has no h1 (R-3 fails in [17] and [50]). It is a near-free fix, 1 unit was left unspent, and nobody built it.
Cycle 2 registered nothing because of the part-type pricing error [36]. It cost no budget but used one of 3 cycles.
The Requester's cut renumbered done-when, so Audit and Identity used old numbers [25][28], causing 3 invalid Audit moves.
The final 'not workable' list [56] includes items 8, 13, 14 and 15, which Audit [51] and the code checks [50] show passing or passing with a warning. It reports 13 problems when about 8 are real.
All four builders said they did not run a browser [15][42][45][48]. Only code checks measured the result.
learnings: Test system: a 40-unit start against a charter of at least 175 [10] makes every run a budget-triage test. Test next with a budget near full price, or a smaller brief, to see whether the department can finish.
Test system: keep done-when ids stable after a Requester drop. Evidence: the 3 invalid Audit moves [28] and the correction in [29].
Test system: do not count 'passes but unpaid' items as problems in the workable list [51][56].
J2 design: give Adaptation and Priority the part-type pricing rule up front (fixes to an existing section are 'fix' parts). Priority should check part type, not just price [31][32-34].

J2 design: run the mechanical check (overflow, h1, JS errors) right after each workflow, or give builders a measuring tool. It found the overflow and the missing h1 only after the whole queue ran [17][50].
Keep: the three-option budget question and the recorded drop list. Test next: Identity should not set funding order [25]; check whether the fix holds.
Evidence is thin on conflict handling: 0 counters, 0 refusals, 0 conflicts, and lessons memory was off. Run with tighter envelopes to exercise the COUNTER and REFUSE paths and the four-hop bargain.
